__NOTOC__
'''Tenno Jinja''' (天王神社、天王社) is a Shinto shrine dedicated to {{ill|Gozu Tennō|en|Gozu Tennō|qid=Q11570247|lt=Gozu Tennō}} and {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}, central deities in {{ill|Gion Faith|en|Gion cult|qid=Q11588425|lt=Gion Faith}}. This name is especially used for shrines in the lineage of {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|en|Tsushima Shrine|qid=Q705136|lt=Tsushima Shrine}} in {{ill|Tsushima, Aichi|en|Tsushima, Aichi|qid=Q816736|lt=Tsushima City, Aichi Prefecture}}. Other shrines based on Gion Faith include {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八坂神社 (曖昧さ回避)}}, {{ill|Gion shrines|ja|祇園神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gion Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11588442}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)}}, {{ill|Yakumo shrine|ja|八雲神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yakumo Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11391847}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社}}, and {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社}}, whose usage varies by era and source.

Currently, only a few shrines still worship Gozu Tennō directly. Most shrines now enshrine {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}, who was syncretized with Gozu Tennō under {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|en|Shinbutsu-shūgō|qid=Q2279088|lt=Shinbutsu-shūgō}}. During the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|en|Shinbutsu bunri|qid=Q1970535|lt=Shinbutsu bunri}} (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) in the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}}, some shrines reverted to deities listed in ancient records other than Susanoo.

Since the Meiji period, many shrines have been merged with others or renamed to align with the Tsushima Gozu Tennōsha, such as renaming to {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|en|Tsushima Shrine|qid=Q705136|lt=Tsushima Shrine}}. As a result of Shinbutsu bunri and shrine mergers, some shrines now enshrine deities other than Gozu Tennō or interpret Gozu Tennō as a deity distinct from Susanoo. In some regions, the influence of these shrines can still be seen in place names incorporating "Tenno."

==Merged second translation==
__NOTOC__
'''Tennō Shrine''' (天王神社) and '''Tennō-sha''' (天王社) are Shinto shrines of the {{ill|Gion Faith|en|Gion cult|qid=Q11588425|lt=Gion Faith}} tradition that enshrine {{ill|Gozu Tennō|en|Gozu Tennō|qid=Q11570247|lt=Gozu Tennō}} and {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}.

It is observed that this name is used in shrines belonging to the lineage of {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|en|Tsushima Shrine|qid=Q705136|lt=Tsushima Shrine}} (Tsushima City, Aichi Prefecture). Other shrine names based on the Gion faith include {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八坂神社 (曖昧さ回避)|lt=Yasaka Shrine}} (also known as {{ill|Q11487447|ja|弥栄神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yaei Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11487447}}), {{ill|Gion shrines|ja|祇園神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gion Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11588442}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|lt=Hiromine Shrine}}, {{ill|Yakumo shrine|ja|八雲神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yakumo Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11391847}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社}}, and {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社}}, names which vary according to the era and source.

Among the current enshrined deities, only a few shrines have {{ill|Gozu Tennō|en|Gozu Tennō|qid=Q11570247|lt=Gozu Tennō}} as their primary deity, while many shrines enshrine {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}, who had been syncretized with Gozu Tennō through {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|en|Shinbutsu-shūgō|qid=Q2279088|lt=Shinbutsu Shūgō}}. During the Meiji era's separation of Shinto and Buddhism ({{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|en|Shinbutsu bunri|qid=Q1970535|lt=Shinbutsu Bunri}}), some shrines reverted to the deities recorded in ancient tradition rather than enshrining Susanoo.

Since the Meiji era, due to joint enshrinement ({{ill|co-Enshrinement|ja|合祀}}) with other shrines and the renaming of institutions such as the Tsushima Gozu Tennō Shrine, many shrines have changed their names to, for example, Tsushima Shrine. Additionally, influenced by the separation of Shinto and Buddhism and such joint enshrinement, there are shrines where the enshrined deity is not {{ill|Gozu Tennō|en|Gozu Tennō|qid=Q11570247|lt=Gozu Tennō}}, and some where Gozu Tennō is interpreted as a deity other than Susanoo. In certain regions, the legacy of this phenomenon can even be seen in local place names bearing "Tennō."
